content: Adverse reactions associated with metronidazole treatment have been documented across various systems of the body. Below is a detailed description of these reactions: Central Nervous System The most severe adverse effects reported in patients treated with metronidazole include convulsive seizures, encephalopathy, aseptic meningitis, and both optic and peripheral neuropathy. Peripheral neuropathy is primarily characterized by numbness or paresthesia in an extremity. Persistent peripheral neuropathy has been observed in some patients undergoing prolonged metronidazole therapy. Patients should be explicitly warned about these potential reactions and instructed to discontinue the medication and consult their physician immediately if any neurological symptoms arise. Additional reported neurological symptoms include headache, syncope, dizziness, vertigo, incoordination, ataxia, confusion, dysarthria, irritability, depression, weakness, and insomnia. Gastrointestinal System The most frequently reported adverse effects involve the gastrointestinal tract. These include nausea, which may sometimes be accompanied by headache, anorexia, and occasionally vomiting. Other gastrointestinal symptoms include diarrhea, epigastric distress, abdominal cramping, and constipation. Oral Cavity A sharp, unpleasant metallic taste is a common complaint. Other oral manifestations include a furry tongue, glossitis, and stomatitis. These conditions may be associated with a sudden overgrowth of Candida species during therapy. Dermatologic Reactions Patients have reported erythematous rash and pruritus. Hematopoietic System Reversible neutropenia (leukopenia) has been observed, and in rare cases, reversible thrombocytopenia has been reported. Cardiovascular System Electrocardiographic changes, such as flattening of the T-wave, have been noted. Hypersensitivity Reactions Hypersensitivity reactions include urticaria, erythematous rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, flushing, nasal congestion, dryness of the mouth (or vagina or vulva), and fever. Renal System Renal adverse effects include dysuria, cystitis, polyuria, incontinence, and a sensation of pelvic pressure. Darkened urine has been reported in approximately one patient per 100,000. The pigment responsible for this phenomenon is likely a metabolite of metronidazole and appears to have no clinical significance. Other Reactions Other reported effects include Candida overgrowth in the vagina, dyspareunia, decreased libido, proctitis, and transient joint pains resembling serum sickness. Rare cases of pancreatitis, which generally resolved upon discontinuation of the drug, have also been reported. Crohn's Disease and Cancer Risk Patients with Crohn's disease are known to have an increased incidence of gastrointestinal and certain extraintestinal cancers. There have been reports in the medical literature of breast and colon cancer in Crohn's disease patients treated with high doses of metronidazole for extended periods. However, a causal relationship has not been established. It is important to note that Crohn's disease is not an approved indication for the use of Flagyl 375 capsules.
